title: Arrest warrant issued for Brandon Aiyuk in connection with misdemeanor speeding charge
content:
The Santa Clara District Attorney’s Office has issued an arrest warrant for San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, according to a court document obtained by The Athletic.

Aiyuk, 28, is sought on a misdemeanor charge of exhibition of speed, according to the district attorney’s office.

The warrant comes after the Santa Clara Police Department launched an investigation into a video that Aiyuk posted online in December 2025 of himself driving more than 100 miles per hour down a street near Levi’s Stadium, where the 49ers play home games and where their team operations and training facility are located. The police sent the case to the district attorney’s office on Jan. 15, a spokesperson for the DA’s office said.

The video quickly went viral after Aiyuk posted it to his YouTube channel. It shows him speeding along California roads with the speedometer showing 111. It is unclear whether the gauge is set to miles per hour (mph) or kilometers per hour (kph). The vehicle he was driving, a Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing, can be set to either mph or kph, and 111 kph would equal 69 mph.

The speedometer even shows speeds over 100 as he approaches the stadium on Tasman Drive, most of which has a 40 mph limit.

Aiyuk apologized days later. “Sorry yall, my car content won’t come with speeding anymore! Was praying with my son tonight and wouldn’t want anybody else to miss out on an opportunity to do the same with their loved ones! My apologies.”

On Wednesday, he posted photos and a video on Instagram of him at a racetrack and a black Mercedes-Benz racing around the track.

Aiyuk has not played since suffering a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus against the Kansas City Chiefs on Oct. 20, 2024.  In January 2026, general manager John Lynch said it was “safe to say” Aiyuk played his last snap with the 49ers and hinted at a potential transaction. But a trade hasn’t happened yet, and neither Aiyuk nor the team has explained why the sides had a falling out.

Aiyuk was a big part of the 49ers’ latest run of reaching the NFC Championship Game three consecutive years and advancing to the Super Bowl in the 2023 season. He caught 209 passes for 3,183 yards and 20 touchdowns in 2021, 2022 and 2023. In 2024, Aiyuk and the 49ers entered into a contract stalemate that dragged on for months before the sides agreed on a 4-year, 120 million extension.
